title: Sources: databases, APIs, files, logs, applications and IoT

videos.script: ana has just joined the data team at Roda Livre. Her first month goes on one question: where does the data come from? {{map}} Six places. A database built to charge customers, and an API at the payments company. A file a contractor drops every night, and the log of a web server. Events from the app, and a sensor in every dock. {{six}} None of them was built for her. Each belongs to somebody else, and each one fails in its own way. {{owners}} In this lesson you build a small copy of each source on your own machine, and you watch it fail. A copy that keeps a ride the app deleted. {{delete}} An API that tells you to slow down and try again in a second. {{rate-limit}} A file loaded while it was still being written. Seven hundred and eighteen rows of a thousand, and no error. {{half-file}} An hour of sensor readings, where more arrived than were due and six are still missing. {{sensors}} Not one of these stops a program. Each one leaves a table that looks complete. {{quiet}} So the lesson ends with questions. The ones to ask a source's owner before the first copy, which become a data contract once they are written down. {{contract}}
